newsitem.title: HONG KONG: AIG unit SPC Credit mandates HK$3 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: AIG unit SPC Credit mandates HK$3 bln loan.

text.p: SPC Credit has mandated three banks as arrangers and bookrunners for a HK$3.0 billion transferable credit facility, Chase Manahattan Bank said Tuesday.
The three banks are Chase Manhattan Asia, Fuji Bank and Standard Chartered Bank.
SPC Credit, which is wholly owned by American International Group (AIG), currently is registered as a deposit taking company under the Hong Kong Banking Ordinance.
The facility consists of three tranches.

Tranche 1 or HK$1.0 billion and tranche 2 of HK$500 million are 364-day revolving credits for both Hong Kong and U.S. dollar drawings, whereas tranche 3 of HK$1.5 billion is a three-year term loan for Hong Kong dollar drawing.
Interest margins are 27 basis points per annum for both tranches 1 and 2 and 40 basis points per annum for tranche 3.
Proceeds of the facility will be used to refinance the company's HK$3.0 billion revolving credit facility due to mature in April 1997.
